author: "Isaac Neuhaus"

After a sequencing run you get a QC table — one row per sample, a dozen metrics — and you need to
answer three questions fast: **which samples fail, is a whole batch off, and are the failures
correlated?** A single scatter can't do it; you want several views that **talk to each other** —
select a suspicious sample in one and see it light up in the rest. In R that usually means Shiny (a
server, reactive wiring). canvasXpress does it client-side: give every panel the same **broadcast
group** and a selection broadcasts to all of them. Here we build a real QC dashboard for 96 RNA/exome
samples.

## The QC table

96 samples with mapping rate, duplication, Q30, GC, insert size and contamination (VerifyBamID
`freemix`), plus lane / batch / library annotations. (Download:
[`ngs-qc.csv`](ngs-qc.csv).)

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

qc <- read.csv("ngs-qc.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
metrics <- c("total_reads", "pct_mapped", "pct_duplication", "pct_q30",
             "gc_content", "insert_size", "contamination_freemix")

m        <- as.matrix(qc[, metrics]); rownames(m) <- qc$sample
annot    <- data.frame(Lane = qc$lane, Batch = qc$batch, Library = qc$library,
                      row.names = qc$sample)
head(qc[, c("sample", "batch", "library", "pct_mapped", "pct_duplication",
            "contamination_freemix")], 4)
```

## Overview — a clustered QC heatmap

Z-score each metric and cluster: outlier samples and any batch/library structure jump out at a
glance. This is the "is anything wrong, and where" view.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data = t(scale(m)), smpAnnot = annot,
  graphType = "Heatmap", samplesClustered = TRUE, variablesClustered = TRUE,
  colorSpectrum = list("navy", "white", "firebrick3"),
  title = "QC metrics (z-scored) — 96 samples clustered",
  width = 820, height = 420
)
```

## The linked triage dashboard

Four panels over the **same samples**, all sharing `broadcastGroup = "qc"`. The sample is the unit,
so each sample is a point (`varAnnot` carries its lane/batch/library). Select points in any panel —
drag a box in a scatter, click a bar — and the same samples re-mark everywhere.

```{r}
qc_panel <- function(cfg, ...) {
  do.call(canvasXpress, c(list(data = m, varAnnot = annot,
                               broadcast = TRUE, broadcastGroup = "qc"), cfg, list(...)))
}
```

### 1 — Mapping rate vs duplication (the triage plot)

Bubble size is depth; failing libraries fall to the **bottom-right** (low mapping, high
duplication). Lasso them here.

```{r}
qc_panel(list(graphType = "Scatter2D", xAxis = list("pct_duplication"),
              yAxis = list("pct_mapped"), colorBy = "Batch", sizeBy = "total_reads",
              title = "Mapping rate vs duplication — select the bottom-right"),
         width = 640, height = 360)
```

### 2 — Contamination vs mapping

```{r}
qc_panel(list(graphType = "Scatter2D", xAxis = list("pct_mapped"),
              yAxis = list("contamination_freemix"), colorBy = "Batch",
              title = "Contamination (freemix) vs mapping rate"),
         width = 640, height = 360)
```

### 3 — Q30 vs GC, by library prep

```{r}
qc_panel(list(graphType = "Scatter2D", xAxis = list("gc_content"),
              yAxis = list("pct_q30"), colorBy = "Library",
              title = "Q30 vs GC content, coloured by library"),
         width = 640, height = 360)
```

### 4 — Sequencing depth per sample

```{r}
qc_panel(list(graphType = "Bar", graphOrientation = "vertical",
              xAxis = list("total_reads"), colorBy = "Batch",
              title = "Total reads per sample (flag the short ones)"),
         width = 820, height = 300)
```

Put the four panels on one page (this document, a Shiny app, a flex layout). Lasso the bad cluster
in panel 1 and panels 2–4 immediately restrict to those samples — you can read their contamination,
their library, and their depth without a single callback. The "wiring" is one shared group id.

## Why "reproducible"

Each panel is a portable `data` + `config` spec; the cross-filter is just a shared `broadcastGroup`.
The same specs reproduce the dashboard from Python or JavaScript, against the same `ngs-qc.csv`.
